To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the legitimacy of CSOs is associated with their agency.
legitimacy with donors and with citizens is positively associated with CSO agency.
CSOs’ agency toward government is associated with legitimacy with both donors and citizens, but not with legitimacy with either group in isolation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether CSOs with different forms of legitimacy are more likely to be effective intermediaries between donors and citizens.
the question of how legitimacy with donors and/or citizens affects CSOs’ agency in the context of governance.
the question of how CSOs can become legitimate with citizens and donors and how this affects agency and outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
legitimacy with citizens is not a sufficient condition for agency and that legitimacy with donors is not a necessary condition for agency.
legitimacy with donors and legitimacy with citizens are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
legitimacy with citizens and donors has an important impact on CSOs’ agency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
legitimacy matters, but it matters differently.
legitimacy with donors, citizens and both are important for civic agency.
legitimacy matters for agency and that CSOs with legitimacy with both donors and citizens are in the best position to develop agency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
legitimacy with citizens and donors are not necessarily mutually exclusive.
legitimacy with citizens and donors are not mutually exclusive.
the relationship between legitimacy, agency and outcomes is not straightforward.
